title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E08 — Death in the Old West
Tales of the Old West are often larger than life and full of improbable adventure, yet a few stories are actually stranger than fiction.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E01 — The Vikings in Medieval History
Hostile Christian sources demonize the Vikings; Muslim accounts render them exotic; revisionist historians belittle the Norse raids; archeological finds combined with a study of the Norse sagas enrich the understanding of Scandinavia's medieval past.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E02 — Land and People of Medieval Scandinavia
Scandinavia's landscape shapes its culture; dense forestation leads to close-knit communities; woodworking and sailing are the key means of long-distance travel; harsh winters engender skill in cold-weather commute; the emergence of great halls.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E03 — Scandinavian Society in the Bronze Age
The physical evidence paints a picture of the Bronze Age in Scandinavia; Viking ancestors trade Arctic goods, amber and slaves in exchange for foreign copper and tin; new wealth fosters larger villages; the beginnings of the Norse pantheon.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E04 — Scandinavia in the Celtic and Roman Ages
Scandinavia survives on trade with the Celts; contact with Rome enriches the upper classes; Scandinavians returning from Roman military service bring back advanced weapons and armor; petty kings and the first Scandinavian sailing ships emerge.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E01 — The Earliest Explorers
The Vivaldi brothers' ill-fated journey to India; what drives the brothers, or drives any explorer, to take a risk and venture into the unknown; theories on how the Pacific islands become populated starting with an epic movement 7,000 years ago.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E02 — The Scientific Voyage of Pytheas the Greek
The originator of scientific exploration treks to the edge of the world so that he can see what is there; putting Pytheas the Greek in the context of his time and place; the Mediterranean as a cradle of civilization; influencing later exploration.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E03 — St. Brendan - The Travels of an Irish Monk
Religious motivations for exploration; the Irish monk St. Brendan sails the Atlantic in a tiny leather boat; he seeks God and flees the world's corruptions; some search for paradise and some for seclusion; a legacy that affects later exploration.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E04 — Xuanzang's Journey to the West
Alarmed at inconsistencies in the Buddhist texts available to him, Xuanzang embarks on an illegal holy pilgrimage to acquire authoritative teachings; he brings Buddhist traditions to the Confucian Chinese; the central character in a classical novel.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E01 — America-The Philosophical Experiment
Although Americans have a reputation as pragmatists, not philosophers, they rely on a framework of political theory grounded in liberalism; an overview of this tradition; establishing a context for exploring and defining American political thought.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E02 — Historical Baggage
The colonies' first European settlers from Great Britain are shaped by ideas of government developed in their home country; exploring the centuries of British political tradition; the forging of a new notion of governance.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E03 — Theoretical Baggage
The historical events of British history help shaped America's definition of government; the colonists are influenced by the Protestantism of Martin Luther and John Calvin and the theory of liberalism developed by Thomas Hobbes and John Locke.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E04 — A Puritan Beginning
The first European colonists sail to the New World to gain freedom to practice their religion; examining how the Calvinist world-view of these settlers dominates early colonial life, as exemplified in the leadership of John Winthrop.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E01 — The American Presidency
The selection of 12 great American presidents who lead the nation through crises; the personal and public lives of the leaders; exploring their presidencies and how they shape both the office of the presidency and the history of the United States.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E02 — George Washington - The Rise of a Patriot
George Washington wants fame and a lasting, positive legacy; by fame, he does not mean mere celebrity, but the honest esteem that comes from service, sacrifice and character; with all of today's debunking cynicism, he remains a true American icon.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E03 — George Washington - American Liberator
During the Revolution, Washington is the indispensable man; he leads the Continental Army to victory against the British; the cause of strengthening a weak national government; in 1788, he is elected as the first president under the new Constitution.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E04 — George Washington - The First President
President Washington has to work to establish precedents and administer the new government; he and his gifted cabinet establish a new financial system, develop a foreign policy based on non-involvement in European affairs and pursue expansion.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E05 — George Washington - American Icon
Washington's second term sees parties forming even as Washington remains above the fray; he deals with threats from abroad and shows the power of the federal union by crushing the Whiskey Rebellion; he refuses a third term and steps down in 1797.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E06 — Thomas Jefferson - The Pen of Freedom
Thomas Jefferson occupies a special place in American history; he has written the Declaration of Independence, the Northwest Ordinance and Virginia's Statute for Religious Freedom; considering his views on women and on slavery.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E07 — Thomas Jefferson - Party Leader
Jefferson is minister to France and later Secretary of State; he loses to John Adams in 1796; Jefferson leads the formation of the Democratic-Republicans. In 1800, he unseats Adams; the first transfer of presidential power in US history.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E08 — Thomas Jefferson - Expansionist President
Jefferson's greatest accomplishment as president, the Louisiana Purchase, comes in his first term; the years also see the first-ever presidential sex scandal when Jefferson is charged with fathering children by his slave, Sally Hemings.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E01 — A Meeting of Two Worlds
Introducing the themes of increasing American power; indigenous political aspirations; conflicting interests and goals; growing mutual antagonism; setting the stage for World War I.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E02 — Wilson & the Breakup of the Ottoman Empire
An examination of wartime and postwar American policy; showing how Wilson's commitment to an ethnocentrically defined view of national self-determination drives his efforts to shape the postwar settlement in the Middle East.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E03 — The Interwar Period
American interest in the Middle East between the wars; revealing one's focus shifting in the 1930s to American interest in Saudi Arabian oil; the increasing activism of American Zionism in response to Hitler's persecution of German Jews.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E04 — U.S. & the Middle East During World War II
United States' entry into World War II alters Americans' conception of the Middle East; the Middle East's geopolitical orientation is now seen as vital to American security.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E01 — A Tale of Two Ancient Cities
Jericho and Anau are two of the world's oldest cities; their stories have much to say about the scope of human history; what makes these cities successful; how they differ from each other; introducing the concept and key themes of Big History.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of Humanity
Tracing the origins of the human species from the emergence of proto-humans to the rise of Homo sapiens, Professor Benjamin offers perspectives to show what makes the human species unique and why it has been able to flourish.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E03 — Foraging in the Old Stone Age
The Paleolithic Era is the longest time in human history; understanding this period is crucial for comprehending the human history that follows, including how family dynamics, migration patterns, climate change and more affect life in this era.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E04 — Origins of Agriculture
Debating why and how humanity transitions from foraging to agriculture; delving into the agricultural revolution; how some combination of climate change, population growth and human ingenuity leads to a revolution in human history.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E01 — Native America: A Story of Survival
The commonly held views of Native Americans and the realities of a tapestry of vibrant cultures; Cobb explains the pitfalls that occur when history does not provide this crucial viewpoint; the mistake of consigning Native Americans to the past.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The Columbian Exchange: New Worlds for All
The misleading dichotomy of Old World and New World impacts perceptions of Native Americans; the Columbian Exchange is the crux behind the creation of new worlds for all; shaping everything from the fauna and flora to the cuisines of the world.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E03 — The Native South and Southwest in the 1600s
The cultures that exist before the Spanish Invasion; the struggle for power through Hernando de Soto's entrada through the Southeast; the Pueblo War for Independence in the Southwest; the Native American worlds born in the aftermath of these events.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E04 — Werowocomoco and Montaup in the 1600s
How connections are forged between Native Americans and newcomers as they incorporate each other into their worlds; examples across the Northeastern Woodlands down to Werowocomoco; how the search for common ground begins at first contact.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E01 — What Is Big History?
Learning whether it is possible to tell a story of everything, from the Big Bang up to the present day; introducing the background and unique aspects of the broad and multidisciplinary perspective on history.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E02 — Moving across Multiple Scales
Most history courses cover time spans of a few decades or a few centuries, but big history requires one to survey the past over scales that span billions of years, becoming familiar with the immense scales needed to cover the modern creation story.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E03 — Simplicity and Complexity
Introducing the development of increasing complexity since the creation of the universe; examining the definition of complexity; learning how the universe builds more complex entities.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E04 — Evidence and the Nature of Science
Learning whether to trust the claims of modern science about events in the distant past; evidence for proving scientific claims; how new dating techniques have allowed scientists to peer further back into the past than previously thought possible.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E01 — Steppes and Peoples
The Mongol sack on Baghdad in 1258 is often seen as the epitome of the clash between barbarian peoples of the steppes and the people of the civilized world; exploring this notion and a detailed account of the destruction; life on the steppes.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of the Steppe Nomads
Learning about the earliest known nomads of the Pontic-Caspian steppes; innovations include the raising of livestock, the domestication of the horse and the invention of the spoked wheel; transforming steppe life and leading to migrations.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E03 — Early Nomads and China
Learning about Indo-Europeans in Mongolia; examining how Iranian and Tocharian nomads come into contact with China; their interaction; the repercussions this contact has across the central and western steppes; the bordering civilizations.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E04 — The Han Emperors and Xiongnu at War
The Xiongnu are promised Chinese brides, among other humiliating and unacceptable gifts; looking closely at the relationship between the Han Empire of China and the nomadic confederacy of the Xiongnu; Han tries to eliminate the Xiongnu threat.

How connections are forged between Native Americans and newcomers as they incorporate each other into their worlds; examples across the Northeastern Woodlands down to Werowocomoco; how the search for common ground begins at first contact.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E01 — What Is Big History?
Learning whether it is possible to tell a story of everything, from the Big Bang up to the present day; introducing the background and unique aspects of the broad and multidisciplinary perspective on history.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E02 — Moving across Multiple Scales
Most history courses cover time spans of a few decades or a few centuries, but big history requires one to survey the past over scales that span billions of years, becoming familiar with the immense scales needed to cover the modern creation story.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E03 — Simplicity and Complexity
Introducing the development of increasing complexity since the creation of the universe; examining the definition of complexity; learning how the universe builds more complex entities.

title: Big History: The Big Bang, Life on Earth, and the Rise of Humanity
description:
S01 E04 — Evidence and the Nature of Science
Learning whether to trust the claims of modern science about events in the distant past; evidence for proving scientific claims; how new dating techniques have allowed scientists to peer further back into the past than previously thought possible.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E01 — Steppes and Peoples
The Mongol sack on Baghdad in 1258 is often seen as the epitome of the clash between barbarian peoples of the steppes and the people of the civilized world; exploring this notion and a detailed account of the destruction; life on the steppes.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of the Steppe Nomads
Learning about the earliest known nomads of the Pontic-Caspian steppes; innovations include the raising of livestock, the domestication of the horse and the invention of the spoked wheel; transforming steppe life and leading to migrations.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E03 — Early Nomads and China
Learning about Indo-Europeans in Mongolia; examining how Iranian and Tocharian nomads come into contact with China; their interaction; the repercussions this contact has across the central and western steppes; the bordering civilizations.

title: The Barbarian Empires of the Steppes
description:
S01 E04 — The Han Emperors and Xiongnu at War
The Xiongnu are promised Chinese brides, among other humiliating and unacceptable gifts; looking closely at the relationship between the Han Empire of China and the nomadic confederacy of the Xiongnu; Han tries to eliminate the Xiongnu threat.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E01 — A Tale of Two Ancient Cities
Jericho and Anau are two of the world's oldest cities; their stories have much to say about the scope of human history; what makes these cities successful; how they differ from each other; introducing the concept and key themes of Big History.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of Humanity
Tracing the origins of the human species from the emergence of proto-humans to the rise of Homo sapiens, Professor Benjamin offers perspectives to show what makes the human species unique and why it has been able to flourish.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E03 — Foraging in the Old Stone Age
The Paleolithic Era is the longest time in human history; understanding this period is crucial for comprehending the human history that follows, including how family dynamics, migration patterns, climate change and more affect life in this era.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E04 — Origins of Agriculture
Debating why and how humanity transitions from foraging to agriculture; delving into the agricultural revolution; how some combination of climate change, population growth and human ingenuity leads to a revolution in human history.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E01 — Native America: A Story of Survival
The commonly held views of Native Americans and the realities of a tapestry of vibrant cultures; Cobb explains the pitfalls that occur when history does not provide this crucial viewpoint; the mistake of consigning Native Americans to the past.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The Columbian Exchange: New Worlds for All
The misleading dichotomy of Old World and New World impacts perceptions of Native Americans; the Columbian Exchange is the crux behind the creation of new worlds for all; shaping everything from the fauna and flora to the cuisines of the world.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E03 — The Native South and Southwest in the 1600s
The cultures that exist before the Spanish Invasion; the struggle for power through Hernando de Soto's entrada through the Southeast; the Pueblo War for Independence in the Southwest; the Native American worlds born in the aftermath of these events.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E04 — Werowocomoco and Montaup in the 1600s
How connections are forged between Native Americans and newcomers as they incorporate each other into their worlds; examples across the Northeastern Woodlands down to Werowocomoco; how the search for common ground begins at first contact.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E01 — Spies: Facts and Fiction
How much pop culture gets wrong about espionage.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E02 — The Human Element
The traits spies should and shouldn't have.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E03 — The Great Game
Heated political games involving Britain, Russia, India, and Afghanistan.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E04 — Beyond the Femme Fatale
The various roles women played throughout history as spies.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E05 — Strange Bedfellows
Uncovering covert and intelligence operations employed during WWII by different countries.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E06 — Making Codes, Breaking Codes
Secret codes may be one of the most interesting and intriguing components of espionage.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E07 — The Mole and the Hunter
Investigating the stories of specific characters in espionage history, such as The Cambridge Five.

title: The Secret World of Espionage
description:
S01 E08 — The Art of Counterintelligence
An operation so secret, even Prime Minister Winston Churchill didn't know about it.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E01 — What Einstein Got Right: Special Relativity
How Einstein's powerful intuition led him astray in several key areas of physics, which are now among the most fruitful areas of the discipline; looking at what he got right, starting with his special theory of relativity.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E02 — What Einstein Got Right: General Relativity
Einstein's general theory of relativity, which built on special relativity and led to a radically new understanding of the geometry of space and time; the rocky road Einstein followed to this breakthrough; the mistakes that hampered his progress.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E03 — Einstein's Rejection of Black Holes
Einstein's rejection of the most astounding prediction of general relativity; how the concept of black holes emerged from Einstein's theory and how he dismissed it, even as other researchers examined the theoretical properties of these objects.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E04 — Einstein and Gravitational Waves
Einstein's reluctance to accept the idea that general relativity predicts that objects with mass radiate extremely faint gravitational waves when they interact; the evidence accumulated after Einstein's death of the existence of gravity waves.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E05 — Cosmology and the Cosmological Constant
Investigating what Einstein reportedly called his biggest blunder, which is his insistence that the universe is static; why general relativity is inconsistent with a static universe; Edwin Hubble's pioneering observations of the cosmos.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E06 — The Cosmological Constant and Dark Energy
Einstein's attempt to make general relativity compatible with a static universe by adding a cosmological constant to his equations; how this mistake looks prescient in light of the discovery that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E07 — What Einstein Got Right: Light Quanta
Retracing the route to Einstein's proof that light is made up of discrete quanta, an insight that led to the quantum revolution; how Einstein broke out of the classical mode of thinking about light and matter through experimentation.

title: What Einstein Got Wrong
description:
S01 E08 — Does God Play Dice with the Universe?
Einstein's devotion to determinism and how it prompted him to reject the probabilistic interpretation of quantum mechanics; Einstein famously saying that "God does not play dice"; how Einstein sought to find a deterministic version of the theory.
